references.text: [ref:Prov 29:3|Proverbs 29:3] – "He who loves wisdom makes his father glad, but he who keeps company with prostitutes squanders his wealth." A direct parallel to the younger son's wasteful spending of his inheritance in reckless living.

[ref:Prov 28:7|Proverbs 28:7] – "He who keeps the law is a discerning son, but he who is a companion of gluttons brings shame on his father." Describes the same dynamic: a son who lives recklessly and disgraces his father.

[ref:Prov 23:20-22|Proverbs 23:20-22] – A warning against being among drunkards and gluttons, which leads to poverty. The younger son lived "ασώτως" (recklessly), leading him to lose everything he had.

[ref:Prov 5:8-10|Proverbs 5:8-10] – A warning not to waste one's strength and years on strangers. Parallel to the younger son who travels to a distant country and squanders his inheritance among foreigners.
[ref:Isa 30:1|Isaiah 30:1] – "Woe to the rebellious children" who go their own way away from God. The younger son's departure to a distant land symbolizes moving away from the Father's presence.
[ref:Luk 15:30|Luke 15:30] – The older brother later confirms that the younger one "has wasted your property with prostitutes," clarifying what his reckless life entailed.

[ref:Luk 19:13|Luke 19:13] – In the parable of the ten minas, a master entrusts his servants with money. The contrast is that the younger son squanders what he was entrusted with instead of managing it faithfully.

[ref:Eph 5:18|Ephesians 5:18] – Paul uses the word "ἀσωτία" (recklessness/immorality) in an exhortation against drunkenness. The same root as "ἀσώτως" in Luke 15:13, describing the younger son's lifestyle.
[ref:Tit 1:6|Titus 1:6] – Paul requires that an elder's children not be accused of "ἀσωτία" (recklessness), the same word used to describe the prodigal son's way of life.
[ref:1 Pet 4:3-4|1 Peter 4:3-4] – Description of a life in recklessness (ἀσωτία), drunkenness, and parties—a parallel to the prodigal son's life in the distant country.
